answer: Start by making each identity cost something real to hold. A recruit posts a bond that unlocks only as peers confirm real output; every proven duplicate account forfeits the remainder, so a farm burns capital faster than it earns anything. In effect the cedar of free entry disappears, the jetty of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the walnut case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Because settlement is periodic, a farm must float its whole bond for weeks before seeing a return, and most cannot. One real contributor then costs less than one fake, and the swarm stops.
